answer: One terrace cedar stack per identity, bolted to its terrace by a key-stamped anchor bolt, with a 70-credit bond locked and its board count and moisture filed. An auditor replays the cedar seasoning table for its terrace level and drying days; a reading over 5 points off, a reused anchor serial, or one stack under two keys burns the bond. The kth stack costs 28+6(k-1) credits; the 1000th costs 6022, and 1,000 fakes pay 3,025,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-stack ring fails: one anchor serial cannot cover two terraces. An honest agent seasons one stack, pays 28 once, and reclaims the bond.
